text:
morgan: quick design ping — I uploaded an experiment for the 'Service metrics' chart in Fig: https://figma.com/file/xyz-series-scale. we have two series: throughput (requests/s) and p95 latency (ms). how should tick labels behave when units mismatch?
elaine: depends on whether we overlay vs dual-axis. are we trying to avoid dual axes?
raja: i'd avoid dual axes unless absolutely necessary — people misread them. can we normalize or show separate mini-axes?
taylor: agree about confusing dual axes. proposal: stack the series (two rows) or add a small unit chip next to series legend and keep a single shared y with normalized percent-of-baseline.
morgan: stacking is okay but dashboard space is tight. normalize-to-baseline might hide absolute values (ops needs ms).
elaine: what about compressed/annotated ticks: show shared percent ticks but on hover tooltip show absolute values with units. so chart stays compact but details available.
raja: +1 to hover details but accessibility concern — screen readers need access to both units without hover.
taylor: for a11y, we can add aria-label text that reads: "series A: throughput x req/s; series B: p95 latency y ms" for the chart element. simple SR-friendly summary beneath the chart as hidden text.
morgan: good call. copy suggestion for hidden text: "Throughput (requests per second) and 95th percentile latency (milliseconds) shown. Hover points for absolute values." any polish on wording?
elaine: tighten to: "Throughput (req/s) and 95th percentile latency (ms). Use hover or data table for exact values"
raja: another problem: outliers in latency distort normalized line. options: cap at 99th percentile, log-scale, or mark outliers and show a secondary y-range toggle.
taylor: i'd avoid log-scale unless the audience understands it. capping + outlier markers seems safest. visual: a faint dashed line at cap value and shaded points flagged as "outlier" in legend.
morgan: how do we communicate capping in legend copy? suggested legend suffix: "(values > X capped to X)" or include a tooltip on the axis label.
elaine: short copy in legend makes it noisy. prefer axis tooltip. maybe add a small info icon next to axis: "Some extreme values capped for visualization — see raw data"
raja: we should also surface the policy in chart settings: Users can toggle "Show raw extremes". default: capped.
taylor: UX nit: when we cap, smoothing (rolling avg) can still be thrown off by the cap. smoothing should compute on raw values but render on capped values? want consistent story.
morgan: technical note for eng: smoothing should be applied on de-noised series (e.g., rolling median) computed on raw data, then render both raw (capped) + smoothed overlay. that preserves trends without letting single spikes blow up scale.
elaine: example snippet for label formatting — use short SI formatter for throughput and plain ms for latency:
```
if (series.unit === 'req/s') formatTicks = siShort(2) // 1.2k
if (series.unit === 'ms') formatTicks = int() + ' ms'
```
raja: also add per-series unit chip in legend: small suffix like "· req/s" and "· ms" so it reads in-line. screen readers should get the unit in the legend item text.
taylor: accessibility copy tweak: legend items read as "Throughput, 12k requests per second" rather than "Throughput 12k". include unit words not abbreviations for SR.
morgan: ownership — @elaine can you update figma with stacked-mini option and the capped+marker treatment? @raja can you draft the accessibility aria snippet? i'll follow up with a short ops doc about default capping at 99th percentile.
elaine: on it, will add variations and annotate constraints (space, export PNG behavior). :pencil2:
raja: will draft aria and example SR text by EOD.
taylor: i'll mock the legend chips and the small axis info icon states.
design-bot: thread summary created: "Series scaling + outlier policy: prefer capping at 99th pct with outlier markers; avoid dual-axis; provide hover & SR-friendly absolute values; add unit chips in legend; smoothing computed on raw then rendered on capped series."
morgan: awesome — thanks everyone. will sync if any blockers. :thumbsup:
